question: Does training-time supervision enrichment add value beyond training-free inference-time context construction for multi-hop KGQA?
description: Co-E is training-free yet reported competitive with larger or trained systems, and the dominant paradigm in the landscape is inference-time context construction. This raises the question of whether a training-time supervision change (context-enriched fine-tuning plus RL) adds value over simply constructing better context at inference, and whether the contribution is a supervision effect or an inference-context effect in disguise.
confidence_basis: Based on a bounded literature set (95 papers retrieved, 10 analyzed) where all context-construction systems are inference-time and no matched-budget training comparison exists; the conclusion rests on absence of evidence plus one controlled inference-time ablation, not on a direct training-time experiment.
rationale: The landscape is saturated with inference-time context methods, several of them training-free and competitive with trained systems; a null or small effect for the training-time intervention would remove most of the idea's contribution.
resolution: Partially resolved, and the resolution is itself the key finding: no retrieved study compares training-time context-enriched supervision against inference-time context construction at matched budget, so the incremental value of training-time enrichment is unmeasured (G001). Indirect evidence cuts both ways: a training-free context system is reported competitive with trained systems (C006), and all analyzed context-construction work operates without retraining (C001, C008), suggesting any training-time advantage may be small; conversely the inference-time ablation is not a training experiment, so it cannot rule out that fine-tuning teaches the model to use context a frozen reader ignores (C015). The question therefore requires the matched-budget, inference-context-matched experiment in G001.
